Under v4's literal words that correct test violated a task-wide, twice-stated rule, so two graders reading the two places could reach opposite verdicts on the same code. This is the same class of self-contradiction planner finding P2 closed in v4 for criteria 1, 2 and 4 while leaving criterion 3 standing.  CORRECTED IN v4, in both directions. v3 wrote this as a rule about defaults rather than about rejections, which (a) forbade the twelve `trustedPaths: []` call sites criterion 5 requires to remain UNCHANGED, since those let the default apply while rejecting nothing, and (b) was contradicted by criteria 1, 2 and 4, each of which drove a rejection with only a verifier injected. The rule, as v5 states it: A REJECTION REQUIRES AN EXPLICIT `onReject`. Input that rejects nothing — an empty list, or a non-empty list the verifier approves in full — is exempt, because nothing is rejected and nothing is written. Criteria 1, 2, 4 and 7 each carry that requirement in their own text as of v4; criterion 3 states its exemption in its own text as of v5.
